title: The knight: the piece that jumps
outcomes: Taps every square a knight can jump to, including captures
Knows the knight is not blocked by pieces in between, unlike rooks and bishops
Tells which pieces can reach a square when nobody names the piece

steps.text: The **knight** moves in an L: two squares along a rank or a file, then one square to the side. It is the only piece that **jumps over** other pieces. It lands on an empty square or captures an enemy piece, but never lands on its own piece. Every jump ends on a square of the opposite colour.

steps.caption: The knight jumps over the ring of pawns. Seven landing squares are open.

steps.text: Rooks, bishops and queens need a clear path. A knight does not: it only needs a landing square that is not held by its own piece. That is why, at the start of a game, a knight can move while most other pieces cannot.

steps.title: A crowd does not stop a knight
steps.prompt: Every back-rank piece is boxed in by pawns. Predict first: which of these can move at the start, the knight on b1 or the bishop on c1?

steps.caption: To reach e5 from g1 the knight needs two jumps: first f3, then e5.

line.say: First jump: from g1 to f3.
Second jump: from f3 to e5.
